sites.name: Tanco Mine (Bernic Lake)
sites.description: Canada's only producing lithium mine and one of the world's largest cesium sources. Operating since 1969; Sinomine bought it in June 2019 for $135M and restarted spodumene production in late 2021. Throughput about 400 t/day.
sites.regulatory_notes: Original licence No. 973 dates from 1983. A cesium plant amendment was filed in 2022 and a 2023 Notice of Alteration allowed milling of ore from other properties. A new comprehensive licence replaced the 1983 one and excluded the proposal to partly drain Bernic Lake. Appeals against the new licence were dismissed by cabinet order — the Wilderness Committee objected not to the licence but to the appeal route, since the only recourse is to the same minister whose department issued it. In 2022 Ottawa ordered three other Chinese firms to divest Canadian lithium assets; Sinomine kept Tanco.

sites.name: Falcon West cesium project
sites.operator_raw: Grid Metals (85%) / Avenir Minerals, an Agnico Eagle subsidiary (15%)
sites.co_owners: Avenir Minerals, an Agnico Eagle subsidiary (15%)
sites.description: Drilled October 2025 to March 2026. About 50,000 t of rock containing roughly 1,300 t of cesium — described by the company as the second-largest cesium deposit to be developed in the Western world, and roughly half of one year's global supply. Small enough that it might be mined out in a year. 130 km east of Winnipeg, 500 m north of the Trans-Canada.
sites.regulatory_notes: An Environment Act licence filing is planned by the end of 2026. Consent from Sagkeeng First Nation has not been given and talks are ongoing; Chief E.J. Fontaine describes the relationship positively and two members have worked as technicians on the prospecting team, while saying environmental concerns and economic benefits still have to be worked out. Note the word used is consent, not consultation. Added from Winnipeg Free Press reporting — this entry did not appear in the underlying research and is the least checked here.

sites.name: Tanco open pit / Bernic Lake drainage concept
sites.description: A 2023 proposal to partly drain Bernic Lake for open-pit access.
sites.regulatory_notes: Explicitly excluded from the replacement licence. Would almost certainly trigger federal permits.

sites.name: Tanco concentrator and cesium plant expansion
sites.commodity: Lithium and cesium concentrates; cesium nitrate and carbonate
sites.description: A CAD 176M, 1 Mtpa processing plant approved in February 2023.
sites.regulatory_notes: Cesium plant expansion filed as an Environment Act Proposal amendment in 2022.

sites.name: Shatford Lake lithium
sites.operator_raw: ACME Lithium, optioned to Snow Lake
sites.description: 31 claims contiguous to the south of Tanco.

sites.name: Donner Lake lithium
sites.description: Spodumene ore test-milled at Tanco under a 2023 Notice of Alteration.

sites.name: Thompson Mine Complex
sites.operator_raw: Vale Base Metals, transferring to Exiro / Orion / Canada Growth Fund consortium (81.1%)
sites.co_owners: transferring to Exiro / Orion / Canada Growth Fund consortium (81.1%)
sites.description: Two underground mines and a mill on the 135 km Thompson Nickel Belt. In February 2026 Vale agreed to transfer majority ownership to a consortium including the federal Canada Growth Fund, with up to US$200M committed.
sites.regulatory_notes: Operates under long-standing provincial licences; no Commission referral was found for the change of control. Vale's Q2 2026 statements still describe Thompson as held for sale, so closing is not confirmed. Nickel, copper and cobalt are all on Canada's critical minerals list.

sites.name: Birchtree Mine
sites.description: Underground mine southwest of Thompson.

sites.name: Pipe Lake deposit
sites.description: Historic Thompson Nickel Belt deposit.

sites.name: Thompson smelter and refinery
sites.description: Former integrated smelter and refinery. Closure dates unverified.

sites.name: Minago Critical Minerals Project
sites.commodity: Nickel, platinum group metals, magnesium, aggregate
sites.operator_raw: Norway House Cree Nation (Minago Development GP)
sites.description: Wholly owned by Norway House Cree Nation since November 2024, bought from Flying Nickel for about $8M plus share surrender. Resource of roughly 690–722 Mlb nickel measured and indicated, plus palladium and platinum. The first phase quarries dolomite for low-emission magnesium before nickel — the community describes this as using the entire animal.
sites.regulatory_notes: Environment Act Licence No. 2981 issued August 2011 to Victory Nickel for a 10,000 t/day open pit. Changes proposed in 2022 triggered consultation with Norway House, Misipawistik, Mosakahiken, Pimicikamak and the Manitoba Métis Federation. The amended licence was announced in March 2026. No Commission hearing was held. Manitoba committed $2M toward the magnesium phase at PDAC 2026. The site lies inside the Norway House Resource Management Area — the one RMA overlap verified in the research. Marketed by the community as removing the usual consultation hurdle through direct ownership.

sites.name: Lalor Mine
sites.description: Anchor of the Snow Lake operations. In September 2026 Hudbay extended reserve life to 2043, with reserves of 27 Mt containing 2.0 Moz gold and production averaging about 185,000 oz/yr.
sites.regulatory_notes: No Commission history found. Zinc concentrate moves by rail to Churchill for export to Europe, 2026 being the third consecutive year.

sites.name: 1901 deposit
sites.description: Satellite deposit adjacent to Lalor.

sites.name: Stall Concentrator
sites.description: Base-metal mill treating Lalor ore.

sites.name: New Britannia Mill
sites.description: Gold mill, restarted 2021.

sites.name: Britannia gold project
sites.description: Past-producing gold mine named as a growth option in September 2026.

sites.name: 777 Mine
sites.description: Hudbay's flagship Flin Flon mine. Closure ended production in the district.
sites.regulatory_notes: Closure obligations updated for the mine site and tailings compound.

sites.name: Flin Flon metallurgical complex
sites.description: Concentrator on care and maintenance. Hudbay is studying flow-sheet changes to reprocess the tailings for critical minerals and precious metals.
sites.regulatory_notes: Wildfires forced a regional evacuation in May 2025.

sites.name: Thompson Brothers lithium deposit
sites.description: Spodumene pegmatite on the Grass River linking Wekusko Lake with Crowduck Bay. Resource figures conflict badly across sources — roughly 8–11 Mt at about 1% Li₂O from company-linked sources; one trade site's 73.6 Mt figure is inconsistent with everything else and should not be used.
sites.regulatory_notes: No Environment Act filing found. The company has renamed repeatedly and pivoted toward uranium elsewhere, so the Manitoba lithium project appears deprioritised.

sites.name: Grass River lithium deposit
sites.description: Second deposit of the Snow Lake lithium project.

sites.name: CentrePort lithium hydroxide plant
sites.operator_raw: Snow Lake Resources / LG Energy Solution
sites.description: Proposed battery materials plant.

sites.name: Gordon deposit (former Farley Lake mine)
sites.description: The higher-grade pit, to be mined first.
sites.regulatory_notes: Federal assessment completed March 2023 with a positive decision statement. Separate provincial licence issued.

sites.name: MacLellan deposit and mill
sites.description: 9,000 t/day mill. About 186,000 oz/yr over a 25-year life, roughly 3 Moz total. Initial capital raised to $937M. First production expected in the first half of 2029, delayed from 2028 by the 2025 wildfire evacuation.
sites.regulatory_notes: Environment Act Licence No. 3391, with a Notice of Alteration approved 26 March 2026. The only Manitoba mineral project in this catalogue to go through a full federal environmental assessment, completed March 2023. Benefit agreements are in place with both proximate First Nations: Marcel Colomb signed in June 2023, Mathias Colomb in 2025 while its judicial review of the federal decision statement was being resolved. No provincial Commission hearing.

sites.name: Lynn Lake legacy mine
sites.description: Farley headframe and mill demolished; tailings cover options under review.
sites.regulatory_notes: One of five priority orphaned and abandoned mine sites under a $50.7M five-year commitment.

sites.name: Ruttan Mine
sites.description: More than 1.3 million cubic metres of clay placed over the tailings.

sites.name: Sherridon / Camp Lake
sites.description: The Sherritt-Gordon mine operated 1931–51 and left about 7 Mt of acid-generating tailings over 47 hectares. Remediation began in 2009 and construction was declared complete in 2022.
sites.regulatory_notes: The province considers this finished; the Manitoba Métis Federation does not. It says many Red River Métis citizens still have concerns, and earlier reporting documented local distrust. Manitoba created a Sherridon Collaboration Table in March 2024. A good test case for whether a closed file is actually closed.

sites.name: Eden Lake carbonatite
sites.description: Manitoba's best-documented rare earth carbonatite occurrence.
sites.regulatory_notes: Note that the Mindat locality for this name is about 110 km off; the provincial coordinates were used.

sites.name: True North Mine and Mill
sites.description: Formerly San Gold, then Klondex. About 62,000 ha and a fully permitted 1,300 t/day mill. A March 2026 preliminary economic assessment outlines about 58,000 oz/yr over 11 years.
sites.regulatory_notes: The restart uses existing permits; no new Environment Act filing was found. First Nation relationships are not documented in the sources consulted — a gap worth closing.

sites.name: Central Mine (Bissett)
sites.description: Historic gold mine, one of five priority legacy sites.

sites.name: Wanipigow sand quarry
sites.description: More than 41 contiguous quarry leases about 160 km north of Winnipeg. Inferred resource of 24.4 Mt of low-iron glass sand.
sites.regulatory_notes: Licence No. 3285 issued 16 May 2019. A Notice of Alteration reducing volume and footprint produced licence 3285 R, approved July 2023 by the department — no Commission hearing. Hollow Water's chief and council supported the project and signed a participation agreement; the Wilderness Committee says they waived Crown consultation. Some members opposed it through Camp Morningstar, citing sacred sites, and criticised the use of a minor alteration to make a substantial change. The cleanest contrast with Sio Silica anywhere in this catalogue.

sites.name: Selkirk glass manufacturing facility
sites.status: Licensed; solar plans on hold, float-glass pivot
sites.description: A 121-acre site on the CP subdivision using Selkirk's wastewater effluent. Up to $880M estimated. In September 2026 the company was promoting a 600 t/day float-glass plant instead, noting Canada has no domestic float-glass production.
sites.regulatory_notes: Provincial approval announced 14 February 2024 — two days before Sio Silica was refused. The environment minister went on record explaining how the two projects differed. Technical reviewers had questioned the company's lack of glass-making experience and whether Wanipigow sand could reach solar purity.

sites.name: SiMbA sand extraction (formerly Vivian / CanWhite)
sites.description: Airlift extraction of silica from the Winnipeg Sandstone aquifer, piped as slurry to a separately licensed plant. The original plan was 1.36 Mt/yr over 24 years from more than a thousand wells, up to 7,200 over time. The aquifer supplies drinking water to about 100,000 people.
sites.regulatory_notes: The only mineral project in the Commission's record. Referred in November 2021 for significant public interest. Twelve hearing days, 27 February to 15 March 2023, in Steinbach, Anola and Beausejour. The June 2023 report made eight recommendations and said the Commission could not state with confidence that the effects were understood — it declined to recommend either way. A draft licence was circulated in September 2023. On 16 February 2024 the minister refused it, saying the risk was simply too great; the company called the decision political. Springfield council voted against twice and was overruled by the Municipal Board; a phone-in referendum ran about 95% against. The Métis Federation intervened. Participants received no funding. Re-filed as SiMbA in October 2025 covering years 0–4 only, with an equity offer to Brokenhead Ojibway Nation reportedly worth more than $10M a year — a First Nation the company had not consulted the first time round. No decision found.

sites.name: Vivian Sand processing facility
sites.description: Processing plant fed by the slurry line.
sites.regulatory_notes: Licensed separately from the extraction project — a split that let one half proceed while the other was contested.

sites.name: Gods Lake Mine
sites.description: Remote fly-in legacy site.

sites.name: Snow Lake historic workings
sites.description: Historic tailings.

sites.name: Baker Patton
sites.description: Listed as a high-priority orphaned site.

sites.name: Keewatinohk Converter Station
sites.description: Northern terminal of Bipole III and the proposed tie-in point for the Kivalliq line.

sites.name: Riel Converter Station
sites.description: Southern terminal of Bipole III.

sites.name: Kelsey Generating Station
sites.description: Built to power the Thompson nickel operations.
sites.regulatory_notes: Probably within the Split Lake Resource Management Area — inferred, not verified.

sites.name: Kettle Generating Station
sites.description: Lower Nelson station.

sites.name: Long Spruce Generating Station
sites.description: Lower Nelson station.

sites.name: Limestone Generating Station
sites.description: Largest Lower Nelson station.

sites.name: Keeyask Generating Station
sites.operator_raw: Keeyask Hydropower Limited Partnership — Manitoba Hydro with four Cree Nations
sites.description: Partnership with Tataskweyak, War Lake, York Factory and Fox Lake Cree Nations.
sites.regulatory_notes: Commission hearings from October 2013 into January 2014, mostly at the Fort Garry Hotel in Winnipeg, with a report in April 2014.

sites.name: Jenpeg Generating Station
sites.description: Controls Lake Winnipeg outflow.
sites.regulatory_notes: Probably within the Cross Lake Resource Management Area — inferred.

sites.name: Port of Churchill
sites.description: The only Arctic deepwater port connected to the North American rail network. Owned by a partnership of 41 Indigenous and Bayside communities, including 29 First Nations. 2026 traffic includes Snow Lake zinc concentrate for a third year, Saskatchewan concentrate, potash and the first grain since 2020.
sites.regulatory_notes: Port of Churchill Plus was referred to the federal Major Projects Office on 11 September 2025 — rail upgrade, icebreaking, an all-weather road and a new energy corridor. Still pre-development. $175M of federal funding over five years announced March 2025.

sites.name: Port Nelson corridor concept
sites.description: Could not be confirmed as an active proposal. Treat as a lead only.

sites.name: Amaranth gypsum
sites.description: Candidate entry, not verified.

sites.name: Gypsumville quarry
sites.description: Candidate entry, not verified.

sites.name: Black Island silica
sites.description: Historic glass-sand source. Not verified.

sites.name: Russell / Gambler potash
sites.description: Candidate entry, not verified.

routes.name: Bipole III
routes.description: HVDC line from Keewatinohk to Riel on a west-side route.
routes.regulatory_notes: Commission hearings October to November 2012, with sessions in Winnipeg, Gillam, Thompson, The Pas, Dauphin, Portage la Prairie and Niverville, plus a route-adjustment session in March 2013. Report June 2013.

routes.name: Manitoba–Minnesota Transmission Project
routes.description: 500 kV line from Dorsey to the US border near Piney.
routes.regulatory_notes: Commission hearings May to June 2017 at the convention centre in Winnipeg; report to the National Energy Board in October 2017.

routes.name: Kivalliq Hydro-Fibre Link
routes.description: About 1,200 km, 150 MW plus fibre, from the Gillam area to five Kivalliq communities in Nunavut and two mines. Cost estimates have risen from $1.6B to $3.39B.
routes.regulatory_notes: Pre-development. Manitoba Hydro has reserved 50 MW and a transmission service request has been filed. No Manitoba Environment Act filing or federal impact assessment file was found. Fox Lake Cree Nation signed a memorandum with the Kivalliq Inuit Association in 2021 but conditions its support on mitigation and benefits. Sources disagree on whether the Manitoba origin is Keewatinohk, the Gillam area, or near Churchill.

routes.name: Hudson Bay Railway
routes.description: The Pas to Churchill. Carries Snow Lake zinc concentrate to tidewater.
routes.regulatory_notes: Owned by Arctic Gateway Group. Part of the Port of Churchill Plus referral to the federal Major Projects Office.

routes.name: PTH 6 corridor
routes.description: Winnipeg to Thompson. The main mining supply road; passes the Minago site.

routes.name: PR 391
routes.description: Thompson to Leaf Rapids and Lynn Lake. Being upgraded for the Lynn Lake gold project.

routes.name: PR 304
routes.description: Pine Falls to Hollow Water and Bissett. Haul route for Wanipigow sand and True North gold.

instruments.name: Route selection
instruments.legal_basis: No statutory basis. The 2021 baseline fieldwork was itself screened by the Review Board and followed a speculative corridor from the draft land use plan.
instruments.takes_in: Engineering and cost constraints; traditional land use and Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit studies; whatever input the proponent chooses to seek.
instruments.can_produce: A preferred corridor and a short list of alternatives.
instruments.assessment_method_label: Weighted scoring — numbers assigned and combined
instruments.assessment_method_note: Assumed to use weighted multi-criteria siting of the kind standard in transmission routing. Not confirmed for this project — and if confirmed, it is the only place on the map where incommensurable things are given numbers and added.
instruments.kind_label: Framing — fixes what later steps can argue about
instruments.note: The only step with no public record, and everything downstream traces back to it.

instruments.name: Transmission service request
instruments.legal_basis: Manitoba Hydro's open access transmission tariff. The governing provision has not been read.
instruments.takes_in: A request for up to 150 MW and a point of interconnection.
instruments.can_produce: Feasibility; required system upgrades.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Power-system modelling. A genuinely technical question with a determinate answer.
instruments.note: Filed 4 November 2025. The filing is confirmed; the tariff basis is not.

instruments.name: Federal funding channels
instruments.legal_basis: Programme terms rather than statute.
instruments.takes_in: Project economics, strategic rationale, Indigenous participation.
instruments.can_produce: Contributions with conditions; prioritisation.
instruments.assessment_method_note: No published appraisal method. Decisions appear as announcements rather than as assessments.
instruments.note: Wide intake, no assessment, almost nothing published. Runs throughout rather than stopping here.

instruments.name: Cabinet designation
instruments.legal_basis: Canadian Energy Regulator Act s.261. Federal law treats Nunavut as a province, so the line very likely is an interprovincial power line.
instruments.takes_in: Cabinet consideration.
instruments.can_produce: Designate, or do not designate.
instruments.assessment_method_note: No criteria are published and no timeline applies. The decision is not an assessment of anything.
instruments.note: The entire federal lane hangs on this one order. None has been made, and nothing has to happen before one could be.

instruments.name: Environment Act Proposal
instruments.legal_basis: The Environment Act ss.11–12; Classes of Development Regulation 164/88; Licensing Procedures Regulation 163/88.
instruments.takes_in: Project description, environmental assessment, alternatives considered.
instruments.can_produce: Filed as complete, or further information required.
instruments.decider: Director or Minister, depending on class
instruments.assessment_method_label: Completeness or conformity check against written criteria
instruments.assessment_method_note: Completeness against the regulation's content requirements, including mapping at 1:50,000 or better.
instruments.note: Above 230 kV is Class 3 and the Minister decides; 115 to 230 kV is Class 2 and the Director does. The voltage has not been published, so the whole Manitoba lane's shape is undetermined.

instruments.name: Planning conformity
instruments.legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.76–85, with s.156 applying the planning provisions to the entire project.
instruments.takes_in: Project description and location.
instruments.can_produce: Conforms; does not conform; variance; or exemption.
instruments.assessment_method_label: Completeness or conformity check against written criteria
instruments.assessment_method_note: Conformity against the text of the applicable land use plan. A yes or no question about a document.
instruments.note: Tested against the regional plan, since the 2023 territory-wide plan was jointly rejected in July 2026.

instruments.name: Energy Regulator review
instruments.legal_basis: Canadian Energy Regulator Act ss.2, 261 and 262, with reasons under s.63. Removed from the Impact Assessment Act's list by SOR/2026-185 on 3 September 2026.
instruments.takes_in: Engineering, routing, environmental and socio-economic effects, Indigenous consultation.
instruments.can_produce: Certificate or permit with conditions, or refusal.
instruments.decider: The Commission and Governor in Council
instruments.assessment_method_note: A public interest determination on a hearing record. Inactive here.
instruments.note: Would be the widest single federal forum available. Inactive because nobody has made the designation order.

instruments.name: Public registry and comment
instruments.legal_basis: The Environment Act s.17, with ss.11(8)(a) and 12(4)(a).
instruments.takes_in: Written submissions from anyone. No content filter appears in the Act.
instruments.can_produce: Comments on the record; objections that may prompt a hearing.
instruments.written_reasons: Owed to objectors where no hearing is held (s.12(6))
instruments.assessment_method_note: None. Submissions are collected, not assessed. Nothing filters what may be said and nothing determines what follows.
instruments.note: Everything can come in and nothing goes out — but s.12(6) compels reasons for the decision NOT to hold a hearing.

instruments.name: Technical Advisory Committee
instruments.legal_basis: Administrative practice. Only a general advisory committee power at s.5.
instruments.takes_in: The proposal, reviewed by each department within its own mandate.
instruments.can_produce: Departmental comments and recommended licence conditions.
instruments.assessment_method_label: Expert judgment within a single mandate
instruments.assessment_method_note: Each department applies its own expertise to its own mandate. There is no step at which the departmental views are weighed against one another.
instruments.note: Each department answers within its mandate. Nothing holds several mandates together.

instruments.name: Crown–Indigenous consultation
instruments.legal_basis: Section 35 of the Constitution Act 1982 and provincial policy, which has not been retrieved.
instruments.takes_in: Potential adverse impacts on asserted or established rights.
instruments.can_produce: A consultation record and accommodation.
instruments.assessment_method_note: A legal test turning on the strength of the claim and the seriousness of the impact. Concerns not attaching to a right fall outside it however strongly held.
instruments.note: A rights channel, not a values channel.

instruments.name: Screening
instruments.legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.86–92 and 157. Section 90(i) makes cumulative impacts mandatory. Section 75(1) bars any regulatory authority from issuing a permit until assessment is complete, and s.75(2) makes any such permit of no force or effect.
instruments.takes_in: The proposal plus public and agency comments.
instruments.can_produce: Review not required; review required; or the project must be modified or abandoned.
instruments.assessment_method_note: A threshold judgment: may the project have significant ecosystemic or socio-economic impacts. Socio-economic sits in the test itself, which is the sharpest contrast with Manitoba.
instruments.note: The only confirmed hard gate on the map, and wider than first recorded: a permit issued in breach is void, not merely irregular.

instruments.name: Minister's screening decision
instruments.legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.93 and 94. Section 94(1)(a)(ii) makes a federal panel the default where the project is partly outside Nunavut.
instruments.takes_in: The Board's screening report.
instruments.can_produce: Proceed; review by the Board, a federal panel or a joint panel; or not proceed.
instruments.assessment_method_note: No published method. The Minister may send a project to review even where the Board found none necessary, and chooses the review body.
instruments.note: Who reviews the project is a discretionary choice made before the review begins.

instruments.name: Clean Environment Commission hearing
instruments.legal_basis: The Environment Act ss.6(5)(b), 12(6) and 7(3). Referral is discretionary; the report is due within 90 days.
instruments.takes_in: Evidence, public presentations, Information Requests, cross-examination.
instruments.can_produce: A public report with recommendations.
instruments.public_record: Yes — reports public, transcripts by practice
instruments.written_reasons: Yes, where recommendations are not incorporated
instruments.assessment_method_note: Adversarial hearing with Information Requests and cross-examination. Among the few methods able to hold several considerations in view at once — and it produces advice, not a decision.
instruments.note: Broad admissibility and compelled reasons on departure — and entirely optional.

instruments.name: Scoping and guidelines
instruments.legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.99 and 101. Draft guidelines must be in both official languages and in Inuktitut, which includes Inuinnaqtun.
instruments.takes_in: Public and agency input on what the assessment should cover.
instruments.can_produce: Guidelines telling the proponent what to assess.
instruments.assessment_method_label: Completeness or conformity check against written criteria
instruments.assessment_method_note: Deliberative scoping against a published draft, open to comment. The same framing move as route selection, done in the open.
instruments.kind_label: Framing — fixes what later steps can argue about
instruments.note: The pairing with route selection is the cleanest comparison on this map.

instruments.name: Federal or joint panel
instruments.legal_basis: NuPPAA s.94(1)(a)(ii)–(iii) and ss.160–162, with the record public under s.123(2).
instruments.takes_in: The whole project, including the Manitoba segment.
instruments.can_produce: A panel report.
instruments.decider: Minister of Environment, or joint appointment
instruments.assessment_method_note: Panel hearing over the whole project, including the Manitoba segment.
instruments.note: The only body anywhere on this map with a mandate over the full 1,200 km corridor.

instruments.name: Review and public hearing
instruments.legal_basis: NuPPAA s.102, under which the hearing is discretionary and may be closed; s.103 factors include (c) the priorities and values of the residents and (f) cumulative effects.
instruments.takes_in: The impact statement, technical review, submissions and oral testimony.
instruments.can_produce: Findings.
instruments.public_record: Yes, though a hearing may be closed
instruments.assessment_method_note: Hearing against a mandatory list of factors, with traditional knowledge admissible under s.103(3). The only method anywhere here that names residents' values as something to be considered.
instruments.note: Section 103(c) makes residents' priorities and values a mandatory statutory factor. Nothing in Manitoba law has an equivalent.

instruments.name: Licensing decision
instruments.legal_basis: The Environment Act ss.11 and 12; s.12.0.1 requires proponent consultation to be considered and s.12.0.2 requires climate to be considered.
instruments.takes_in: The assessment record, departmental comments, the consultation record, and any Commission report.
instruments.can_produce: Licence with conditions, or refusal.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Judgment on the record against two named statutory factors. How those are weighed against anything else is not specified and not published.
instruments.note: Everything becomes one answer here. Section 12.0.2 gives climate a statutory foothold no other value in this Act enjoys.

instruments.name: Minister's decision and certificate
instruments.legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.105–111, reconsideration under s.112. Override grounds are limited to national or regional interest, or to terms being insufficient or excessively onerous. Section 107(1) requires the Board to reconsider in light of the Minister's reasons. Section 108 permits the Minister to vary terms that are purely socio-economic.
instruments.takes_in: The Board's report.
instruments.can_produce: Accept or reject terms; override; issue a certificate.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Judgment on the Board's report, with enumerated override grounds — except for socio-economic terms, which s.108 allows the Minister to vary without stating one.
instruments.note: The sharpest thing on this map. Socio-economic considerations are mandatory at review under s.103(c), then singled out at s.108 as the one class of term a Minister may vary without stating a ground.

instruments.name: Water licence
instruments.legal_basis: Nunavut Waters and Nunavut Surface Rights Tribunal Act, s.37 coordinating it with the Review Board.
instruments.takes_in: Water use and waste deposit.
instruments.can_produce: A licence with conditions.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Technical standards and licence conditions.
instruments.note: Whether a transmission corridor triggers it at all is unconfirmed.

instruments.name: Inuit Owned Land access
instruments.legal_basis: The Nunavut Agreement. The relevant articles and the association's lands policy have not been retrieved.
instruments.takes_in: Applications to use Inuit Owned Land parcels.
instruments.can_produce: Permit or lease with terms, or refusal.
instruments.decider: The regional Inuit association, as landowner
instruments.assessment_method_note: Negotiation between landowner and proponent. Whatever is traded against what leaves no public trace — and this may be where the most consequential combining actually happens.
instruments.note: NuPPAA defines a regulatory authority as a public body, so the s.75 gate may not bind a private landowner — while s.74 still prohibits carrying out the project before assessment.

instruments.name: Archaeology permit
instruments.legal_basis: Territorial archaeological and palaeontological site regulations. Not retrieved.
instruments.takes_in: Proposed ground disturbance.
instruments.can_produce: A permit with conditions.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Standards and permit conditions.
instruments.note: Unverified. No party in the record has raised heritage as a concern.

instruments.name: Fisheries Act authorisation
instruments.legal_basis: The Fisheries Act. The provision has not been confirmed.
instruments.takes_in: Works likely to harmfully alter fish habitat.
instruments.can_produce: Authorisation with offsetting, or refusal.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Habitat standards with offsetting requirements. One value, assessed well, and nothing else admitted.
instruments.note: Subject to the Nunavut screening gate, which binds federal authorities in the territory.

instruments.name: Migratory Birds Act
instruments.legal_basis: The Migratory Birds Convention Act 1994. Inferred.
instruments.takes_in: Works affecting birds or nests.
instruments.can_produce: No project permit; constraints on timing.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Prohibitions and timing windows rather than an assessment.
instruments.note: Unverified.

instruments.name: Notice of Alteration
instruments.legal_basis: The Environment Act s.14 (alteration of a licensed development).
instruments.takes_in: A licensee's description of a proposed change to a licensed development.
instruments.can_produce: Approval of a minor alteration (licence amended, e.g. 3285 R), or a direction to file a new proposal.
instruments.public_record: Partial — approvals are posted; the request often is not
instruments.assessment_method_note: The Director decides whether a change is minor enough to approve without a new proposal. No public comment period is required for a minor alteration.
instruments.note: Added 8 Oct 2026 to record mineral-project histories (Wanipigow, Tanco, Minago, MacLellan). Legal basis to be confirmed by Eric.

instruments.name: Appeal to the Minister
instruments.legal_basis: The Environment Act s.27 (appeal of a Director's decision to the Minister).
instruments.takes_in: Written appeals from anyone affected by a licence decision.
instruments.can_produce: Appeal dismissed, or the licence varied or revoked.
instruments.assessment_method_note: Appeal goes to the minister whose department issued the licence. No independent tribunal.
instruments.note: Added 8 Oct 2026 for the Tanco licence appeals. Legal basis to be confirmed by Eric.

instruments.name: Federal environmental / impact assessment
instruments.legal_basis: Canadian Environmental Assessment Act 2012 (projects begun before 28 Aug 2019) or the Impact Assessment Act; triggered by the Physical Activities / Project List regulations.
instruments.takes_in: Environmental impact statement, public and Indigenous comments, agency analysis.
instruments.can_produce: Decision statement with binding conditions, or a finding of unjustified significant effects.
instruments.decider: Minister of Environment and Climate Change (Governor in Council if effects are significant)
instruments.assessment_method_note: Whether the project is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects, after mitigation.
instruments.note: Added 8 Oct 2026 for the Lynn Lake gold project (decision statement March 2023). Distinct from fed-cer, which is the Energy Regulator route for the Kivalliq line.
